items.label: Profile
items.content: Marketing leader with 9+ years building demand generation and revenue-linked growth for B2B SaaS, home-services, and consumer brands. Builds repeatable go-to-market engines end to end: ICP definition, positioning, multi-channel paid acquisition, and attribution that ties spend to booked revenue rather than vanity traffic. Repeatedly cut acquisition cost and cost per qualified lead while lifting conversion and deal quality (CAC $85 to $17, CPL $300 to $90, ROAS 3.6x to 5.8x). Comfortable owning a number, building executive reporting and forecasts, and partnering directly with a founder or CEO.

header.name: Brayden Clark
header.title: Head of Marketing | Demand Generation & Revenue-Linked GTM

body: I am applying for the Head of Marketing role. I build revenue-linked demand generation engines for B2B SaaS and field-service businesses, including a home-services contractor where I shifted the funnel from raw lead volume to booked, completed jobs through a custom ServiceTitan integration and raised ROAS from 3.6x to 5.8x. That is exactly the demand-that-converts, not vanity-traffic mandate this role describes.

I have built go-to-market motions from scratch and rebuilt them at scale. At an AI-first land-acquisition SaaS I owned the full GTM motion (ICP, positioning, channel strategy, and an attribution framework that hit target KPIs), and across a 90+ location brand I rebuilt the marketing function with executive reporting dashboards and cut tracked acquisition cost from $72 to $22. In full-funnel performance work I have driven CAC from $85 to $17 and cost per qualified lead from $300 to $90, landed a $100k per year partnership, and led full rebrands, all while working hand in hand with founders and owners.

PaintScout stands out to me: a founder-led, profitable SaaS with real product-market fit, building the operating system for professional painting contractors. I have done a lot of this work in trades and home services, from plumbing to window washing, and I think in systems rather than silos. I would focus on making growth intentional and measurable, keeping Marketing and Sales in lock-step, and building a durable engine that turns interest into qualified, well-forecasted pipeline.
